scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
aliases: SC Post Matric Scholarship; Post Matric Scholarship SC; PMS SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice & Empowerment)
implementing_agency: State Governments/UT Administrations through National Scholarship Portal (NSP); funds released by Centre to States
launched_year: 1944 (pre-independence scheme, revised many times)
active_period: Continuous; major revivals FY 2016-17, 2017-18, 2019-20 and 2024-25 onward
predecessor: Pre-independence post-matric scholarship for Scheduled Castes; guidelines revised 2016, 2019 and 2024
target_groups: Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD, including professional, technical and vocational courses)
age_criteria: No specific age limit
income_limit: Family annual income up to Rs 2,50,000 from all sources
other_eligibility: Student must belong to a Scheduled Caste; must be enrolled in a recognised post-matriculation course (Class 11/12, ITI, polytechnic, diploma, UG, PG, professional degree) in a government-recognised institution in India; scholarship is payable only for the prescribed duration of the course; student must not hold any other centrally funded scholarship for the same period
exclusions: Students who fail to promote to the next class lose the scholarship; only two members of a family can get this (and other such) scholarships simultaneously; distance/correspondence courses allowed only if the institution is recognised and there is no regular course available; income certificate and caste certificate from competent authority are mandatory
benefits_summary: Reimbursement of all compulsory non-refundable fees (tuition, admission, exam, etc.) charged by the institution plus a monthly maintenance allowance. Also covers study tour charges (up to Rs 1,600 p.a.), thesis typing/printing (up to Rs 1,600 for PhD), book grant, and coaching for competitive exams for courses of less than one year; paid by DBT into Aadhaar-linked bank account
benefit_amount: Maintenance allowance (per month): Group-1 courses (Medicine/Engineering/Agriculture degree, MBA/MCA/LLB) hosteller Rs 1,200 (day scholar Rs 550); Group-2 (Pharmacy, Nursing, B.Ed., Mass Comm., etc.) hosteller Rs 820 (day scholar Rs 530); Group-3 (BA/BSc/BCom general, BBA, BCA) hosteller Rs 570 (day scholar Rs 300); Group-4 (Class 11-12, ITI, polytechnic, vocational) hosteller Rs 380 (day scholar Rs 230). Full compulsory fees paid
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 Centre:State for most States; 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States (100% central for UTs without legislature)
coverage: Largest SC scholarship scheme - about 60 lakh SC students covered per year; over Rs 20,000 crore disbursed in the last decade
application_mode: Online only through the National Scholarship Portal (state schemes may also run on state portals)
documents_required: Caste certificate from competent authority; income certificate (family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh); Class 10/previous exam marksheet; Aadhaar; Aadhaar-seeded bank account in student's name; admission/fee receipt; bonafide certificate; institute verification; passport-size photo
helpline: NSP helpline 0120-6619540 (helpdesk@nsp.gov.in); State social welfare/welfare department helplines
key_features: Oldest and biggest SC education scheme; covers full course fee plus stipend; 100% DBT; applies from Class 11 up to PhD; also gives coaching fees for short courses; renewed every academic year
recent_updates: Income ceiling raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2.5 lakh (2019); maintenance rates revised upward; Aadhaar payment-bridge mandatory; Ministry has pressed States to clear arrears of scholarship dues to institutions since 2024-25
source_1: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment - Scheme list | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes
source_3: PIB / Department of Social Justice annual report content on PMS-SC

scheme_name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students studying in Classes IX and X
aliases: SC Pre Matric Scholarship; Pre-matric scholarship Class 9 10 SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: States/UTs through National Scholarship Portal
launched_year: Post-independence central scheme; current design from 2012-13, rates revised in 2019-20
target_groups: SC students studying in Class IX and X
age_criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines
income_limit: Parental/guardian annual income up to Rs 2,50,000
other_eligibility: SC student studying in government, government-aided or recognised private school in Class 9 or 10; must appear for the prescribed annual examination; attendance and promotion norms apply
exclusions: Not for students in other classes; can be combined with other scholarships subject to ceiling rules; requires income certificate
benefits_summary: Monthly scholarship to reduce drop-out between upper primary and secondary stage and to help SC students reach the post-matric stage, credited by DBT
benefit_amount: Day scholars Rs 225 per month and hostellers Rs 525 per month (for 10 months in a year) as per revised central norms; some States top up the amount
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States)
coverage: Over 40 lakh SC students annually (Central + State share)
application_mode: Online through National Scholarship Portal; school verification compulsory
documents_required: Caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account of student; admission proof; class promotion certificate; photo
helpline: NSP helpline 0120-6619540
key_features: Covers only Classes 9 and 10; paid for 10 months a year; hostellers get more than day scholars; delivered entirely by DBT
recent_updates: Rate revision 2019 (day scholar Rs 225, hosteller Rs 525); income ceiling Rs 2.5 lakh; States advised to pay in one or two instalments per year

scheme_name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Children of those engaged in occupations involving cleaning and prone to health hazards
aliases: Pre-matric scholarship children of manual scavengers; unclean occupation scholarship
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: States/UTs through National Scholarship Portal
launched_year: Long-running scheme; revised guidelines from 2012-13 and revised rates 2019-20
target_groups: Children of persons engaged in unclean/health-hazardous occupations notified under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (tanners, flayers, waste pickers, sewer and septic tank cleaners, etc.) - open to all castes/religions
age_criteria: Students of Classes I to X
income_limit: No income limit (occupation-based eligibility)
other_eligibility: Parent/guardian must be engaged in a notified unclean occupation as per the 2013 Act; child studying in Class I to X in a recognised school; application with occupation certificate
exclusions: Not applicable to children whose parents are not in the notified occupations; cannot draw two scholarships of the same nature
benefits_summary: Monthly scholarship for Classes I-X plus ad-hoc grant for books, uniforms and stationery to enable children of sanitation workers to complete school
benefit_amount: Approximately Rs 110-700 per month depending on class and day-scholar/hosteller status, plus an ad-hoc annual grant (about Rs 750-1,250) for books and stationery; amounts revised periodically - confirm current rates on NSP
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 NE and Himalayan States)
coverage: Lakhs of children of sanitation workers/sweepers annually
application_mode: Online through National Scholarship Portal
documents_required: Occupation certificate of parent/guardian (from local body); Aadhaar; bank account; admission proof; school certificate; photo
helpline: NSP helpline 0120-6619540
key_features: No income ceiling - eligibility is by parent's occupation; covers Classes I to X (unlike the general SC pre-matric scheme which covers only IX-X); intended to break inter-generational manual scavenging
recent_updates: Occupations list aligned with the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013; NAMASTE (2022) now also supports such families

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme of Top Class Education for Scheduled Caste Students
aliases: Top Class Education SC; Top Class Scholarship SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: Ministry's Top Class Education Cell / directly to institutions and students
launched_year: 2007-08 (revised guidelines 2021 and after)
target_groups: Meritorious SC students admitted to premier Indian institutes (IITs, IIMs, NITs, AIIMS, NLUs, IISERs and other institutions identified by the Ministry)
age_criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines
income_limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000 (earlier Rs 6,00,000)
other_eligibility: SC student who secured admission to a notified premier institute for a full-time prescribed degree/diploma course; must not have availed any other scholarship for the same purpose
exclusions: Only notified institutes and courses are covered; benefits are not available for correspondence/distance courses
benefits_summary: Full tuition and non-refundable fees, living expenses for the entire course duration, plus annual book grant and one-time computer purchase assistance
benefit_amount: Full tuition/non-refundable fees; living allowance about Rs 2,220 per month for hostellers (about Rs 1,110 per month for day scholars); book/stationery grant about Rs 3,000 per year; one-time computer purchase assistance about Rs 45,000 - confirm current rates with the Ministry/institute
funding_pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme)
coverage: About 1,000 fresh SC students every year (1,250 in some years) in about 265 identified premier institutes
application_mode: Online application to the Ministry's portal/institute nodal officer after admission; institute certification
application_portal: scholarships.gov.in (NSP) / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Top Class Education portal
documents_required: Caste certificate; income certificate; admission letter of premier institute; fee receipt; Aadhaar and bank details; Class 12 marksheet; institute endorsement
helpline: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, New Delhi
key_features: Covers boarding and lodging along with tuition at top institutes; separate from the mass Post-Matric scheme; supports SC students at IIT/IIM/AIIMS level
recent_updates: Income ceiling raised to Rs 8 lakh; institute list expanded; payments routed through the institute to avoid delays

scheme_name: National Overseas Scholarship for Scheduled Castes, DNTs and landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans
aliases: National Overseas Scholarship SC; overseas scholarship for SC students
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment with Indian missions abroad
launched_year: 1954 as overseas scholarship for SC (present design from 2000s; guidelines revised 2019 and later)
target_groups: SC and DNT students and students from families of landless agricultural labourers and traditional artisans
age_criteria: Below 35 years (and below 40 years for PhD)
income_limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000
other_eligibility: At least 60% marks in the qualifying degree; admission to a Master's/PhD/post-doctoral course in a university abroad (QS top-500 universities prioritised); must give an undertaking to return to India after course completion
exclusions: Only one child per family can get the award; the award is not for undergraduate courses; scholars must return to India within 30 days of completing the course
benefits_summary: Full tuition fees, annual maintenance allowance, airfare, visa fees, medical insurance and contingency grant for study abroad
benefit_amount: 125 awards per year (115 SC, 6 DNT, 4 landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans); 30% of slots reserved for women; maintenance allowance USD 15,400 per year (GBP 9,900 per year for UK) plus full tuition and other grants - confirm current currency rates and ceilings
funding_pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme)
coverage: 125 new scholars every year
application_mode: Online application on the dedicated NOS portal
documents_required: Caste certificate; income certificate from Revenue Officer (not below Tehsildar); degree marksheets; unconditional admission offer letter; valid language-test score; passport; bank details
helpline: Overseas Scholarship Cell, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, New Delhi
key_features: Highly competitive, fully funded foreign education scholarship exclusively for SC/DNT candidates; 30% slots for women; covers top-500 QS universities; includes return-and-serve expectation
recent_updates: Selection cycle opened for 2025-26 with 125 slots; provisional selection lists published on the portal; majority of awards now to STEM and professional courses

scheme_name: National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students
aliases: National Fellowship for SC; Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship SC (old name)
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with UGC as implementing agency)
implementing_agency: University Grants Commission (UGC)
launched_year: 2005-06 as Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship; renamed and revamped in 2012-13 and again 2019-20
predecessor: Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for SC Students (2005-06)
target_groups: SC students pursuing MPhil/PhD in Indian universities and institutions
age_criteria: As per UGC norms for MPhil/PhD admission
income_limit: No income limit, but the candidate should not be employed/ receiving other fellowship during the course
other_eligibility: SC candidates who have registered for MPhil/PhD in a UGC-recognised university/institution; selection on the basis of merit in the qualifying Post-Graduate degree
exclusions: Candidates already receiving another fellowship or salary are not eligible for the same period; fellowship lapses on failure to submit progress reports
benefits_summary: Monthly fellowship for MPhil (limited period) and PhD (full duration), plus HRA/hostel allowance and contingency/annual grant for research expenses; DBT-based
benefit_amount: Fellowship as per UGC rates (about Rs 37,000 per month in the initial two years as JRF and about Rs 42,000 per month thereafter for PhD) plus HRA and contingency grant of about Rs 12,000-25,000 per year; about 2,000 fellowships offered per year for SC students
funding_pattern: 100% Central
coverage: About 2,000 new SC fellowships per year; thousands of ongoing fellows
application_mode: Online through the National Fellowship portal (UGC/Social Justice & Empowerment)
documents_required: Caste certificate; PG degree marksheet; PhD/MPhil registration proof; bank details; undertaking; guide/university endorsement
helpline: UGC helpdesk; Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment fellowship desk
key_features: Merit-based research fellowship for SC students; supports full PhD duration; paid directly to scholar's bank account; aims to increase SC representation in teaching and research
recent_updates: Fellowship rates revised in line with UGC revision; slots increased to about 2,000 per year; digital onboarding through DBT

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana
aliases: PM AJAY; Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana; PMAGY SCA SCSP merged scheme
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: State Governments, District Administrations, State SC Development Corporations, NIRF-ranked institutions
scheme_type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme (100% central assistance to States/UTs)
launched_year: FY 2021-22 (merged three older schemes)
active_period: 2021-22 to 2025-26 (extended with the 15th Finance Commission period; continuing)
predecessor: Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP); Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY); Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY)
target_groups: SC families living below the poverty line; SC-majority villages; SC students needing hostels in top institutions
age_criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines
income_limit: Income Generating and Skill Development components - SC families below the poverty line; infrastructure component - SC-majority villages
other_eligibility: Three components: (1) Adarsh Gram - villages with more than 40% SC population and total population of 500 or more; (2) Grants-in-aid for district/State-level projects including infrastructure in villages with 50% or more SC population and Comprehensive Livelihood Projects; (3) Construction/repair of hostels in institutions funded by Central/State/UT Governments and ranked under NIRF
exclusions: Villages and beneficiaries must be selected through the State/District Annual Action Plan on the PM-AJAY portal; projects outside the approved plan are not eligible
benefits_summary: Integrated development of SC-dominant villages (drinking water, sanitation, education, health, roads, livelihood); grants for livelihood and skill projects for BPL SC families; financial support of up to Rs 50,000 or 50% of asset cost (whichever is less) per beneficiary for livelihood assets; hostel construction in top institutions
benefit_amount: Adarsh Gram component: gap-filling grants per village. Livelihood component: asset grant up to Rs 50,000 or 50% of cost per beneficiary household. Fund shares: up to 50% for Adarsh Gram, up to 2% for hostels, up to 5% for administration/monitoring. At least 15% of grants are to be used for income-generating schemes for SC women, at least 10% for skill development and up to 30% for infrastructure
funding_pattern: 100% central assistance (Centrally Sponsored Scheme; States meet implementation establishment costs)
coverage: 29,881 villages covered under the Adarsh Gram component, of which 6,087 villages have been declared 'Adarsh Gram'; over Rs 3,242 crore released for livelihood projects benefiting over 8.5 lakh beneficiaries
application_mode: Through States/Districts (Annual Action Plans uploaded on the PM-AJAY portal); beneficiaries identified by State/District administration and Panchayati Raj institutions
documents_required: For beneficiaries: caste certificate, BPL/income proof, Aadhaar, bank account, project proposal. For institutions: DPR, NIRF ranking certificate, proof of government funding
helpline: PM-AJAY Programme Implementation Unit, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; State SC Development Corporations
key_features: Umbrella scheme merging SCA-SCSP, PMAGY and BJRCY; creates model 'Adarsh Grams' in SC-majority villages; 50 monitorable socio-economic indicators; builds hostels in NIRF-ranked institutions; earmarks 15% for SC women
recent_updates: Village eligibility widened from 50% to more than 40% SC population in the revised guidelines; 6,087 villages declared Adarsh Gram; hostel component restricted to top-ranked government-funded institutions

aliases: Inter-caste marriage incentive central; Dr Ambedkar inter-caste marriage scheme

launched_year: 2013 (revised guidelines 2020-21)

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
aliases: Venture Capital Fund SC; IFCI SC fund
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: IFCI Ltd. as sponsor/asset management company; fund registered with SEBI under AIF Regulations 2012
launched_year: 2014-15 (initial corpus Rs 200 crore; fund size later enhanced to about Rs 500 crore)
target_groups: SC entrepreneurs and SC-majority companies (manufacturing and services)
age_criteria: 18 years and above (promoter)
income_limit: No income limit (enterprise-based)
other_eligibility: Company/enterprise with at least 51% SC shareholding and management control (12 months for loans above Rs 50 lakh; 6 months for loans up to Rs 50 lakh); manufacturing or services sector with asset creation; SC promoters must retain at least 51-60% stake until exit
exclusions: Trading-only and non-asset-creating proposals; promoters unwilling to bring the prescribed margin (25%)
benefits_summary: Concessional equity/quasi-equity financing for SC entrepreneurs to set up or expand businesses and create jobs
benefit_amount: Assistance from about Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore per company. Up to Rs 5 crore: fund invests up to 75% of project cost, promoters bring 25%. Above Rs 5 crore: fund invests up to 50%, at least 25% from bank/FI and 25% from promoters
funding_pattern: 100% Government of India corpus through IFCI-managed SEBI-registered fund
interest_rate: Concessional - as decided by the Asset Management Company (below market rates; subsidy on interest considered in evaluations)
repayment: Structured exits over about 6 years (equity/quasi-equity with defined exit)
coverage: Loans of about Rs 354 crore sanctioned to 98 SC entrepreneur companies across 17 States (evaluation data); portfolio includes solar power, food processing, packaging and hotels
application_mode: Online application and appraisal by IFCI/the fund manager
documents_required: Caste certificate of promoters; shareholding pattern proof; project report/DPR; audited financials; bank sanction letter for the loan portion; KYC and company registration documents
helpline: VCF-SC / IFCI Ltd., New Delhi
key_features: Largest dedicated venture/equity fund for SC entrepreneurs; loans from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore; preference to SC women entrepreneurs; managed professionally by IFCI under SEBI AIF rules
recent_updates: Fund size enhanced; renewed push in 2024-26 towards technology-driven manufacturing ventures; scheme reviewed for expanding outreach to smaller towns

implementing_agency: IFCI Ltd./designated nodal agency providing credit guarantees to banks
launched_year: 2014-15 (budget announcement 2014; operational from 2015-16)

age_criteria: 18 years and above
income_limit: Normally linked to the definition of SC families within income limits for credit schemes (verify current norm)

exclusions: Defaults and wilful non-repayment lead to guarantee invocation and recovery action; not a subsidy
benefits_summary: Guarantee cover to banks so that SC entrepreneurs with viable projects can get credit without collateral, improving access to institutional finance

funding_pattern: 100% Central
interest_rate: Not applicable (guarantee fee instead of interest)
repayment: As per the underlying bank loan
coverage: Cumulative guarantee support to SC entrepreneurs across States since 2015-16
application_mode: Application routed through the lending bank to the nodal agency (IFCI)
documents_required: Caste certificate; SC shareholding proof; project report; bank appraisal/loan sanction details; financial statements; KYC documents
helpline: IFCI Ltd. / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
key_features: Addresses the biggest barrier for SC entrepreneurs - collateral; works with banks rather than as a subsidy; complements VCF-SC and NSSH
recent_updates: Being dovetailed with other SC entrepreneurship schemes (VCF-SC, National SC-ST Hub) in recent budget announcements; verification of current limits advised

scheme_name: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation - Term Loan Schemes
aliases: NSFDC loan scheme; SC corporation loan; term loan for SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: NSFDC through State SC Development Corporations/Channelizing Agencies, regional rural banks and public sector banks
scheme_type: Corporation credit scheme (Government company under Section 8 of the Companies Act)
launched_year: 1989 (NSFDC set up; renamed from National Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation)
predecessor: National Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (1989)
target_groups: SC families living below double the poverty line (DPL) - artisans, petty traders, transport operators, small entrepreneurs, women
age_criteria: 18 to 55 years (relaxable for specific schemes)
income_limit: Annual family income up to double the poverty line (DPL) as notified (about Rs 1.5 lakh rural / Rs 1.8 lakh urban in recent norms - confirm current DPL)
other_eligibility: SC individual/SHG/cooperative with viable income-generating activity; applications routed through State Channelizing Agencies or partner banks; no existing default with any bank/FI
exclusions: Wilful defaulters; activities prohibited under applicable law; applicants above income ceiling
benefits_summary: Concessional term loans (up to 90-95% of unit cost) for self-employment and income-generating activities, with training and market support
benefit_amount: Term loan up to Rs 30 lakh per unit (Small loans up to Rs 1 lakh; Medium Rs 1-5 lakh; Large Rs 5-30 lakh); beneficiaries pay about 5-6% interest; NSFDC charges State agencies a lower rate
funding_pattern: NSFDC equity from Government of India; on-lending through State Channelizing Agencies
interest_rate: About 5% to 6% per annum for beneficiaries (differs by scheme category and State agency)
repayment: Monthly/quarterly instalments over 3 to 10 years including moratorium, depending on the scheme
coverage: Large portfolio - NSFDC has financed lakhs of SC beneficiaries since 1989 (ask for the current sanction/disbursement figures on the NSFDC dashboard)
application_mode: Offline/online application through State SC Development Corporation (Channelizing Agency) or designated bank branch; some schemes via the NSFDC portal
documents_required: Caste certificate; income certificate / DPL certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; project/unit estimate or quotation; SHG or firm registration if applicable; no-dues declaration
helpline: NSFDC head office, New Delhi (011-26179448); State SC Development Corporation helplines
key_features: Apex Government of India credit institution for SCs; interest well below market rates; works through State channel agencies; combines credit with skill training and market linkage; covers micro-credit to large term loans
recent_updates: NSFDC has expanded digital application, credit-guarantee tie-ups and the Green Business Scheme (e-rickshaw, solar pumps, poly houses) in 2024-26

scheme_name: NSFDC Green Business Scheme
aliases: Green Business Scheme; e-rickshaw loan SC; solar pump loan SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: NSFDC through State Channelizing Agencies
launched_year: 2016 (in response to climate-change concerns and to promote green livelihoods)
target_groups: SC persons setting up green/climate-friendly micro-enterprises
age_criteria: 18 years and above
income_limit: Family income within double the poverty line
other_eligibility: SC applicant proposing activities such as e-rickshaw, solar pump, solar-powered implements, poly-house, waste recycling; unit cost within the prescribed limit
exclusions: Diesel-based or non-green activities; defaulters
benefits_summary: Concessional loan for green livelihood assets, generating income with low running cost
benefit_amount: Loan for unit cost up to about Rs 1 lakh at concessional interest (about 5% per annum)
funding_pattern: NSFDC refinance through State Channelizing Agencies
repayment: Term loan over about 3 to 5 years with moratorium
coverage: Thousands of green livelihood units financed; e-rickshaw financing is the largest segment
application_mode: Through State SC Development Corporation / Channelizing Agency
documents_required: Caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; quotation/invoice of the asset; driving licence for e-rickshaw
helpline: NSFDC head office; State SC Development Corporation
key_features: Ties SC livelihood support to clean energy transition; low unit cost hence easier entry for first-generation entrepreneurs
recent_updates: Expanded in 2024-26 with solar pump and e-mobility financing in rural districts

Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme. Launched: 2016 (in response to climate-change concerns and to promote green livelihoods). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Income limit: Family income within double the poverty line. scheme_name: NSFDC Educational Loan and Vocational Education & Training Loan Scheme
aliases: NSFDC education loan; vocational training loan SC
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: NSFDC through State Channelizing Agencies and banks
launched_year: Educational loan scheme revised through the 2010s; VETLS introduced for short-term courses
target_groups: SC students pursuing professional/technical education and short-term vocational courses
age_criteria: 18 to 55 years
income_limit: Family income within double the poverty line (relaxed for some courses)
other_eligibility: SC student with confirmed admission to a recognised professional/technical course (in India or abroad) or a short-term vocational training course
exclusions: Courses not recognised by the relevant regulator; students with existing education-loan default
benefits_summary: Concessional education loan covering course fees and related expenses for professional/technical education, and small loans for short-term vocational training
benefit_amount: Educational loan as per NSFDC norms (up to Rs 15-30 lakh for professional courses in India/abroad depending on the scheme); VETLS loan about Rs 4 lakh for short courses with 4% interest for male and 3.5% for female awardees
funding_pattern: NSFDC refinance through State Channelizing Agencies
interest_rate: About 4% per annum for men and 3.5% per annum for women under VETLS; concessional rates for education loans
repayment: Starts after six months of completing the course or on employment, whichever is earlier (VETLS); education loans have longer repayment with moratorium
coverage: Thousands of SC students financed for professional and vocational courses
application_mode: Through State SC Development Corporation / Channelizing Agency
documents_required: Caste certificate; income proof; admission letter/fee receipt; academic marksheets; co-obligant details if required; Aadhaar and bank account
helpline: NSFDC head office; State SC Development Corporation
key_features: Interest concession for women; supports both degree-level professional courses and short-term employable training; complements the Post-Matric Scholarship for students outside the income ceiling
recent_updates: Convergence with Skill India/PM-DAKSH short-course skilling in recent years

scheme_name: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation schemes
aliases: NSKFDC loan; safai karamchari loan scheme; sanitation worker credit
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: NSKFDC through State Channelizing Agencies, banks and NGOs
scheme_type: Corporation credit scheme (Government of India company)
launched_year: 1997 (NSKFDC incorporated)
target_groups: Safai karamcharis (sanitation workers) and their dependents, and persons engaged in manual scavenging identified under law - predominantly SC but open to all such workers
age_criteria: 18 to 55 years (relaxable in specific cases)
income_limit: Family income within prescribed limits (about double the poverty line / low-income households)
other_eligibility: Safai karamchari or dependent/legal heir; proposed activity should be viable; applications routed through State Channelizing Agencies or banks
exclusions: Wilful defaulters; activities without income-generation potential; non-target groups
benefits_summary: Term loans at concessional rates for self-employment, small business, transport, education and skill up-gradation; also sanitation-related enterprise finance
benefit_amount: Term loans up to Rs 30 lakh depending on the scheme (Small up to Rs 1 lakh; Medium up to Rs 5 lakh; Large above Rs 5 lakh); interest about 5-6% per annum for beneficiaries; VETLS-type short-term loans with 3.5-4% interest
funding_pattern: NSKFDC equity from Government of India; refinance through SCAs and banks
repayment: 3 to 10 years in monthly/quarterly instalments with moratorium
coverage: Lakhs of sanitation workers and their families financed; ~Rs 1,000+ crore loan portfolio over the years
application_mode: Through State Channelizing Agencies/direct lending through banks; application form on the NSKFDC portal
documents_required: Safai karamchari certificate/employment proof; caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; project report; identity proof
helpline: NSKFDC head office, New Delhi; State Channelizing Agency helplines
key_features: Only national corporation dedicated to sanitation workers' credit needs; includes education loans for children of safai karamcharis; prioritises liberation from hereditary sanitation work
recent_updates: Coordinated with NAMASTE (2022) and the SRMS rehabilitation scheme; NSKFDC supports capital subsidy and skill components of NAMASTE

scheme_name: Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (now under NAMASTE)
aliases: SRMS; NAMASTE scheme; rehabilitation of manual scavengers scheme
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for the NAMASTE sewer/septic tank component)
implementing_agency: NSKFDC and State Governments/Urban Local Bodies
launched_year: SRMS 2007 (revised 2013); NAMASTE launched in 2022-23 as the upgraded umbrella
predecessor: National Scheme for Liberation and Rehabilitation of Scavengers (NSLRS, 1992)
successor: NAMASTE - National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (2022)
target_groups: Identified manual scavengers, sewer/septic tank workers (sanitation workers) and their dependents
age_criteria: 18 years and above
income_limit: No separate income ceiling - eligibility based on identification as manual scavenger/sanitation worker
other_eligibility: Person identified/verified as a manual scavenger or sewer/septic tank worker (or dependent), with a certificate from the district administration; one-time rehabilitation assistance applies once per family
exclusions: Families that have already received the one-time cash assistance under SRMS; persons not in the verified list unless newly identified
benefits_summary: One-time cash assistance, skill training, concessional loans/entrepreneurship support, education support for children, and mechanised sanitation equipment (NAMASTE) for sanitation workers' safety and dignity
benefit_types: Cash assistance; Skill; Loan; Livelihood; Education; Occupational safety
benefit_amount: One-time cash assistance of Rs 40,000 per identified manual scavenger (SRMS); loans up to Rs 15 lakh for sanitation enterprises with capital subsidy up to Rs 5 lakh (NAMASTE/NSKFDC norms); NAMASTE also funds PPE kits, mechanised cleaning equipment and safety devices; budget for NAMASTE components enhanced in recent Union Budgets
funding_pattern: Central assistance with State/ULB participation; NSKFDC as the financial intermediary
interest_rate: Concessional on loans (about 4-5% per annum for beneficiaries)
repayment: As per the linked loan scheme (3 to 10 years)
coverage: Over 1 lakh manual scavengers identified and given rehabilitation assistance since 2013; NAMASTE targets safety and mechanisation for all sanitation workers in urban local bodies
application_mode: Through District Administration/Municipal bodies and State Channelizing Agencies; applications verified against the national survey list
documents_required: Manual scavenger/sanitation worker identification certificate; caste certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; income/project details; dependant proof if applicable
helpline: NSKFDC / NAMASTE helpline; State Sanitation/Social Welfare Department
key_features: Rehabilitation (not just compensation) of sanitation workers; covers cash, skill, credit, education and safety equipment; implemented jointly with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs after 2022
recent_updates: NAMASTE launched in 2022-23 with mechanised cleaning, PPE and enterprise support; Union Budget 2025-26 enhanced sanitation-worker welfare and capital subsidy components

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
aliases: SC ST PoA implementation scheme; atrocity relief scheme; special courts scheme
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
implementing_agency: State Governments/UTs, police, special courts and district administrations
launched_year: 1989 Act; supporting scheme funded continuously since the 1990s (revised guidelines 2016 and later)
target_groups: SC and ST victims of atrocities and their dependents; institutions enforcing protective laws
age_criteria: Not applicable
income_limit: No income ceiling for relief to atrocity victims
other_eligibility: Victim must be an SC/ST person covered under the PCR Act 1955 or the SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989; relief is based on the offence category under the PoA Rules (47 listed offences); FIR/police report and court/medical documentation required
exclusions: Relief amounts differ by offence and may be paid in instalments; the scheme funds institutions, not a general grant for individual applicants
benefits_summary: Financial relief and rehabilitation for atrocity victims and dependents, incentive for inter-caste marriages involving SC/ST victims, funds for special courts, special public prosecutors, protection cells and atrocity-prone-village preventive measures
benefit_types: Legal-relief; Rehabilitation; Cash assistance; Institutional support
benefit_amount: Relief range of Rs 85,000 to Rs 8.25 lakh depending on the offence (e.g. Rs 5 lakh for rape, Rs 8.25 lakh for gang rape/acid attack or murder; Rs 1 lakh for caste abuse/denial of entry), payable within 7 days of the incident in stages; States may pay higher (Tamil Nadu raised to Rs 1-12 lakh). A government task force has recommended raising these amounts for inflation
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 50:50 Centre:State for most components; 100% for some components (special courts, prosecutors) as per guidelines
coverage: Relief paid to tens of thousands of atrocity victims/dependents; special courts and exclusive special courts established in States/UTs
application_mode: Through police, district administration/District Magistrate (relief), and State Social Welfare Department; courts can also order relief
application_portal: https://socialjustice.gov.in (SC/ST PoA scheme); State SC/ST protection cells
documents_required: FIR/crime records; caste certificate of victim; medical report where applicable; identity proof; bank account; dependants' proof; court orders if available
helpline: State SC/ST Protection Cell; National Commission for Scheduled Castes; District Magistrate's office
key_features: Funds the entire protective-legal architecture for SC/ST communities; 47 offence categories mapped to relief amounts; 7-day mandate for first instalment; includes preventive measures in atrocity-prone villages; inter-caste marriage incentive for SC/ST victims is a separate component
recent_updates: Task force (report submitted July 2026) recommended inflation-linked enhancement of relief amounts, counselling for victims/accused, relief cells in every State/UT and 24-hour reporting of FIRs/chargesheets to officials

scheme_name: Eklavya Model Residential Schools
aliases: Eklavya schools; EMRS tribal residential school
state_ut: All India (tribal blocks and areas with 50%+ ST population)
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs; construction with States/UTs
launched_year: 1997-98 (as a scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs); revamped as a Central Sector Scheme from 2018-19 with NESTS
target_groups: ST students, especially from remote tribal areas and PVTG habitations
age_criteria: School students from Class VI to Class XII
income_limit: No income ceiling; eligibility based on ST status and residence in tribal areas; selection test/merit per State norms
other_eligibility: Normally one EMRS in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons; admission for Classes VI and XI (vacancies in other classes where available)
exclusions: Non-ST students are not eligible; students must reside in the school hostel
benefits_summary: Free, high-quality residential education from Class VI to XII with boarding, lodging, books, uniforms, sports and extra-curricular facilities, plus skill and vocational modules
benefit_amount: Fully funded school education - no fees; about 728 EMRS to be functional by March 2026, serving about 3.5 lakh tribal students; recurring cost per student met by the Centre
funding_pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme); States provide land and some infrastructure
coverage: About 440 EMRS operational (2023) and about 700+ sanctioned; target of 728 functional schools with 3.5 lakh students by March 2026
application_mode: Online admission test/application notified by NESTS/State tribal department each year
documents_required: ST (caste/tribe) certificate; domicile/residence proof; Class V/VIII marksheet or school certificate; Aadhaar; photograph; income certificate (where required by State)
helpline: NESTS/EMRS helpline, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (011-23073706)
key_features: Flagship residential school network for tribal children; curriculum includes tribal culture and vocational skills; nationally administered through NESTS; over 600 EMRS students cleared IIT-JEE/NEET-type exams in recent years
recent_updates: 40 new EMRS inaugurated in 2024-25 with foundations for 25 more; target to make 728 EMRS functional by March 2026; large share of new schools located in PVTG blocks

scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students
aliases: ST post matric scholarship; post matric scholarship tribal students
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: State Governments/UTs through the National Scholarship Portal and DBT Tribal portal
launched_year: Long-standing scheme (post-independence era); norms revised from 2012-13, rates revised 2019-20
target_groups: ST students from Class XI to post-graduate and professional courses
age_criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines
income_limit: Family annual income up to Rs 2,50,000
other_eligibility: ST student pursuing any recognised course whose minimum qualification is matriculation (Class X) or above, in a recognised institution in India
exclusions: Student must not draw any other centrally funded scholarship; failure to pass/promote leads to loss of scholarship; Aadhaar-linked DBT compulsory
benefits_summary: Full compulsory course fees plus monthly maintenance allowance, book grant and study-tour support for ST students in secondary and higher education
benefit_amount: Maintenance allowance about Rs 230 to Rs 1,200 per month depending on course group and hosteller/day-scholar status, plus compulsory non-refundable fees; about 30 lakh ST students covered across all scholarship schemes annually
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 Centre:State (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States)
coverage: About 1.01 crore beneficiaries and Rs 13,380+ crore disbursed during 2019-20 to 2024-25; Rs 2,598 crore released in FY 2024-25 alone
application_mode: Online through the National Scholarship Portal / DBT Tribal portal with State verification
documents_required: ST certificate; income certificate (up to Rs 2.5 lakh); Class 10 marksheet; admission proof and fee receipt; Aadhaar-seeded bank account; Aadhaar; photo
helpline: State Tribal Welfare Department; NSP helpline 0120-6619540
key_features: Largest ST education scheme by expenditure; 100% DBT; covers professional courses as well as general degrees; Ministry has repeatedly urged States to clear pending fee dues
recent_updates: Rs 2,598 crore released in FY 2024-25 vs Rs 2,669 crore in FY 2023-24; States instructed to settle institutional dues through DBT; NSP integration strengthened

scheme_name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (Classes IX and X)
aliases: ST pre matric scholarship; tribal pre-matric scholarship class 9 10
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: States/UTs through the National Scholarship Portal
launched_year: 1990s; revised from 2012-13 with rates revised in 2019-20
target_groups: ST students studying in Classes IX and X
age_criteria: Age-appropriate for Classes IX and X
income_limit: Parental annual income from all sources up to Rs 2,50,000
other_eligibility: ST student in Class IX or X in a government/government-recognised school; regular attendance and appearance in the annual examination
exclusions: Only Classes IX and X are covered; no other centrally funded scholarship of the same nature can be held simultaneously
benefits_summary: Monthly scholarship to help ST students continue from upper-primary to secondary stage and reduce drop-out
benefit_amount: Rs 225 per month for day scholars and Rs 525 per month for hostellers, for 10 months in a year (revised rates); annual book grant as applicable
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States)
coverage: About 30 lakh ST students get scholarships annually across all Ministry scholarship schemes; pre-matric covers lakhs of Class IX-X students
application_mode: Online through the National Scholarship Portal with school verification
documents_required: ST certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; school admission proof/promotion certificate; photo
helpline: State Tribal Welfare Department; NSP helpline 0120-6619540
key_features: Only for Classes IX and X; higher rate for hostellers; income ceiling Rs 2.5 lakh (raised from earlier limits); fully DBT
recent_updates: Central funds released: Rs 308.60 crore in FY 2023-24 and Rs 163.69 crore in FY 2024-25; States asked to speed up verification on NSP

scheme_name: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students
aliases: National Fellowship ST; Top Class Scholarship ST; ST research fellowship
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: Ministry of Tribal Affairs directly (Central Sector Schemes) through DBT
launched_year: Fellowship component running since 2000s with new design from 2019-20; Top Class Scholarship from 2013-14
predecessor: Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for ST (earlier design)
target_groups: Meritorious ST students pursuing higher education in premier institutes (Top Class) and MPhil/PhD (Fellowship)
age_criteria: As per institute norms for the course
income_limit: Fellowship - no income ceiling; Top Class Scholarship - family income up to Rs 6 lakh per annum
other_eligibility: Fellowship: 750 fresh ST scholars per year selected on merit in the Master's degree for MPhil/PhD, with preference to girls, divyangjan and PVTG candidates. Top Class: admission to prescribed courses in about 252-265 identified premier institutes (IITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NITs etc.)
exclusions: Candidates receiving another fellowship/salary cannot hold this fellowship; award requires submission of progress reports
benefits_summary: Monthly fellowship for research scholars and, under the Top Class component, tuition and living allowance for ST students in premier institutions
benefit_amount: Fellowship: MPhil Rs 25,000 per month and PhD Rs 28,000 per month (as per latest rates) plus contingency; 750 fresh fellowships per year. Top Class: full tuition, living expenses, book grant and computer allowance, income ceiling Rs 6 lakh
funding_pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Schemes)
coverage: 750 fresh fellowships per year; about 1,000 fresh Top Class scholarships per year; results/merit lists published annually on the Ministry portal
application_mode: Online through the National Fellowship portal/Digital Bharat portal; merit lists published by the Ministry
documents_required: ST certificate; PG degree marksheets; admission/registration proof; bank details; Aadhaar; undertaking and guide's endorsement; income certificate for the Top Class component
helpline: Ministry of Tribal Affairs fellowship desk; 011-23073706
key_features: Two-in-one scheme covering premier-institute scholarships and research fellowships; preference to girls, divyang and PVTG students; paid directly to scholars via DBT
recent_updates: Applications invited for the 2025-26 cycle (closing 31 October 2025); list of eligible institutes expanded to 252; merit lists published on the Ministry site

launched_year: Running since the 2000s; guidelines revised in 2019-20 and later
target_groups: ST students pursuing Master's, PhD and post-doctoral courses abroad
age_criteria: As per the scheme guidelines (normally below 35 years for Master's and below 40 for PhD)
income_limit: Family income ceiling as prescribed in the scheme guidelines (verify current ceiling)
other_eligibility: ST candidate with a good academic record and confirmed admission to a recognised foreign university for a prescribed Master's/PhD/post-doctoral course; must return to India after completion
exclusions: Undergraduate courses are not covered; award is subject to the annual slot ceiling
benefits_summary: Financial assistance covering tuition, maintenance, airfare, visa and related costs for higher studies abroad

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP)
aliases: Van Dhan Yojana; PMVDY; MSP for minor forest produce; TRIFED tribal livelihood
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (implemented through TRIFED)
implementing_agency: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED) and State agencies/State tribal development corporations
launched_year: PMVDY launched 14 April 2018; MSP for MFP operational from 2013-14; both consolidated into PMJVM from 2021-22
predecessor: Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (2018) and the Scheme of MSP for Minor Forest Produce (2013-14)
target_groups: Tribal gatherers of minor forest produce (MFP), tribal artisans, tribal entrepreneurs and SHGs
age_criteria: Not applicable
income_limit: No income ceiling; intended for tribal MFP gatherers and artisans
other_eligibility: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) are formed as clusters of 15 tribal SHGs with about 300 members each; Value Chain Development Centres process and market MFP; MSP procurement through State agencies
exclusions: Non-tribal producers are not eligible for MFP MSP support; benefits flow through SHG clusters
benefits_summary: MSP-backed procurement of minor forest produce, value addition and market linkage for tribal products, e-commerce/retail support (Tribes India) and micro-enterprise training for tribal SHG clusters
benefit_types: Livelihood; Marketing; MSP support; Skill; Enterprise
benefit_amount: MSP notified for 50+ MFPs (2021) including tendu, bamboo, honey, lac, gums; VDVKs get working capital of about Rs 15 lakh per cluster; allocation under PMJVM raised to about Rs 380 crore in FY 2025-26 (from about Rs 152 crore)
funding_pattern: 100% Central through TRIFED and State agencies
coverage: Thousands of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras established and lakhs of tribal gatherers supported; MFP MSP procurement has moved thousands of crores into tribal households since 2013-14
application_mode: Through State Tribal Development/Cooperation Departments; SHG clusters registered as VDVKs; procurement through designated MSP centres
documents_required: ST certificate; SHG membership; bank account; MFP produce records; artisan/vendor registration for Tribes India
helpline: TRIFED, New Delhi; State Tribal Development Department
key_features: Guarantees a minimum price for forest produce so tribal gatherers do not face distress sales; VDVK cluster model converts SHGs into producer companies; Tribes India retail/e-commerce channel; PMJVM merges MSP and Van Dhan
recent_updates: Van Dhan integrated with PMJVM to build tribal producer companies; 50 MFPs covered by MSP; allocation for PMJVM raised to Rs 380.40 crore in FY 2025-26; ongoing tie-ups for tribal product exports

scheme_name: Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs
aliases: tribal vocational training centres; skill development tribal youth
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: States/UTs, NGOs and empanelled training institutions
launched_year: Long-running scheme; revised grant norms in the 2010s and 2020s
successor: Complemented by PM-DAKSH and DAJGUA skill interventions
target_groups: ST youth, especially school dropouts and those in remote areas
age_criteria: Youth eligible for vocational courses (generally 18-35 years, as per course norms)
income_limit: No strict income ceiling (targeted at tribal youth)
other_eligibility: ST youth enrolled in short-term vocational courses in trades with market demand; training institutions receive central grants per trainee
exclusions: Non-tribal youth; courses without placement/market linkage are discouraged
benefits_summary: Free short-term vocational training in trades like computers, tailoring, carpentry, driving, welding, beauty services etc., with stipend, toolkits and placement assistance
benefit_amount: Central grant per trainee for training (roughly Rs 15,000-25,000 per trainee per course) plus stipend and toolkit assistance; thousands of trainees per year across States
funding_pattern: 100% Central (grant to States/institutions/voluntary organisations)
coverage: Thousands of ST youth trained annually; VTCs operate in tribal districts across States
application_mode: Applications through State Tribal Welfare Departments/VTCs; trainee selection by local committees
documents_required: ST certificate; age proof; education certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; photograph
helpline: State Tribal Welfare Department; Ministry of Tribal Affairs
key_features: Short-duration, employability-focused courses; toolkits provided to help trainees become self-employed; prioritises tribal youth from remote habitations
recent_updates: Skills component reinforced under DAJGUA (2024-29) with long-term skilling for ST youth after Class 10/12 and linkage with Skill India Mission

scheme_name: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme
aliases: Forest Rights Act; FRA patta; tribal land rights scheme
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (policy) with Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and States
implementing_agency: State Governments, Forest Rights Committees (village/block/district level), Revenue and Forest Departments
scheme_type: Statutory framework with central support for implementation
launched_year: Act passed 2006; came into force 31 December 2007; rules amended 2012
target_groups: Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers
age_criteria: Not applicable
income_limit: No income ceiling
other_eligibility: Forest dwellers who have lived in forests for at least three generations (75 years) and depend on forests for livelihood; individual rights (homestead, cultivation) and community rights (community forest resource, grazing, minor forest produce, conversion of pattas)
exclusions: Claims must be supported by evidence and recommended by the Gram Sabha and Forest Rights Committee; unsupported claims rejected
benefits_summary: Legal recognition of individual and community forest rights including land titles (pattas), rights over minor forest produce, community forest resource management and rehabilitation in case of displacement
benefit_types: Land rights; Livelihood; Community rights; Legal
benefit_amount: Rights-based (no cash grant). About 24-25 lakh individual titles and over 1 lakh community titles recognised since 2008; title holders can access DAJGUA support for agriculture, animal husbandry and fishery under FRA pattas
funding_pattern: Central support for implementation and digitisation; State Governments execute the process
coverage: About 25 lakh titles distributed cumulatively; digitisation of claims and records ongoing
application_mode: Claim filed with the Gram Sabha/Forest Rights Committee; verification at block and district level; titles issued by the district administration
documents_required: Proof of residence and dependency on forest; Gram Sabha resolution; village records; Aadhaar
helpline: State Tribal Development Department / District FRA cell
key_features: Legal right (not a benefit scheme); Gram Sabha is the primary authority; community forest resource rights allow villages to protect and manage forests; digitisation and FRA cells being funded under DAJGUA
recent_updates: DAJGUA includes digitisation and support to FRA claim processes, FRA cells and community forest resource management plans (2024-29); Forest Rights Act claims accelerated in 2024-26 with district-level monitoring

scheme_name: Establishment of Ashram Schools in Tribal Sub-Plan Areas
aliases: ashram school scheme; tribal ashram shala
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: State Governments/UTs and voluntary organisations
launched_year: Scheme of Ashram Schools running since the 1970s-80s (guidelines revised 2017 and later)
target_groups: ST students, including PVTG and girls, in tribal sub-plan areas
age_criteria: School-going children (primary to higher secondary)
income_limit: No income ceiling
other_eligibility: ST children in remote tribal areas without schools; ashram schools provide residential education with boarding and lodging; State/VO must follow prescribed norms on staffing and facilities
exclusions: Non-ST children except where State rules permit a small non-ST proportion
benefits_summary: Free residential schooling (boarding and lodging) with tuition support for ST children in remote tribal areas
benefit_amount: Central assistance of about Rs 40,000-50,000 per child per year (norm for recurring and non-recurring costs as per guidelines), released to States/voluntary organisations
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - Central assistance with State share (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States in certain components)
coverage: Thousands of ashram schools across tribal sub-plan States, educating lakhs of ST students
application_mode: Application to the ashram school through the State Tribal Welfare Department; admissions notified locally
documents_required: ST certificate; age proof; residence proof; Aadhaar; school records; medical certificate
helpline: State Tribal Welfare Department
key_features: Complements EMRS in remote areas; boarding and lodging free; run by State Governments and voluntary organisations; especially important for PVTG children
recent_updates: DAJGUA (2024-29) includes improving infrastructure of ashram schools and hostels; States being funded to upgrade facilities and add seats

aliases: tribal hostels scheme; ST girls hostel

implementing_agency: State Governments/UTs, universities and voluntary organisations
launched_year: Running since the Third/Fourth Five Year Plan era; guidelines revised 2017 and later
target_groups: ST students (priority to girls) studying in middle, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities away from home
age_criteria: School/college-going students
income_limit: As per State norms for hostel admission (low-income ST families prioritised)
other_eligibility: ST students from rural and remote areas pursuing education; hostels constructed by State Governments, universities or voluntary organisations with central assistance
exclusions: Only ST students; seats allotted as per State rules
benefits_summary: Construction and maintenance of hostels with mess, study rooms and common facilities so that ST students, particularly girls, can pursue education
benefit_amount: Central assistance per hostel bed/block as per scheme norms (about Rs 2.75 lakh per seat under newer hostel construction norms, especially under PM-JANMAN/DAJGUA); repair and maintenance grants also provided
funding_pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 50:50 Centre:State (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States in prescribed components)
coverage: Lakhs of hostel seats created for ST boys and girls over decades; PM-JANMAN adds 500 hostels for PVTG students
application_mode: Applications for hostel seats to the institution/State department; construction proposals through State Annual Action Plans
documents_required: ST certificate; admission proof of institution; income proof; Aadhaar; bank account; photograph
helpline: State Tribal Welfare Department; institution hostel office
key_features: Addresses the biggest cause of ST dropout - distance from school; priority to girls' hostels; PM-JANMAN/DAJGUA are adding new hostels with higher unit costs
recent_updates: PM-JANMAN constructing 500 hostels at about Rs 2.75 crore each; DAJGUA includes setting up hostels in schools at district/block level (2024-29)

helpline: Ministry of Tribal Affairs grant-in-aid desk

recent_updates: Guidelines emphasise online application and timely utilisation certificates; priorities aligned with DAJGUA/PM-JANMAN focus areas

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
aliases: SC ST Hub; National SC ST Hub; MSME SC ST hub scheme
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
implementing_agency: National SC-ST Hub office; NSIC, SIDBI, NABARD, industry associations, IITs/management institutes
launched_year: 2016 (launched by the Prime Minister in October 2016; extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26)
target_groups: SC/ST owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and SC/ST entrepreneurs
age_criteria: 18 years and above
income_limit: No income ceiling (enterprise-based scheme)
other_eligibility: MSME with Udyam Registration (or willing to register) having at least 51% SC/ST ownership; manufacturing, service, trading or agri-allied enterprise for most components; for SCLCSS - SC/ST ownership above 51% with institutional loan for new plant and machinery
exclusions: Non-SC/ST majority enterprises; second-hand machinery (for capital subsidy); dual benefit from a similar subsidy is not allowed
benefits_summary: Capacity building and training, Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (SCLCSS), procurement support to meet the 4% government procurement mandate, GeM and Single Point Registration assistance, reimbursement of bank loan processing fees, exhibition/marketing support and mentorship
benefit_types: Subsidy; Training; Marketing; Procurement support; Credit facilitation
benefit_amount: Capital subsidy of 25% on institutional loan for plant and machinery, capped at Rs 25 lakh (SCLCSS); up to 90% of course fee capped at Rs 1 lakh for training reimbursements; up to 80% of pledge/bank-guarantee charges capped at Rs 1 lakh for tender participation; 100% subsidy on NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme fees
funding_pattern: 100% Central (outlay about Rs 588 crore for 2021-22 to 2025-26)
interest_rate: Not applicable (interest is as per the lending bank's rate; subsidy reduces capital cost)
repayment: As per the institutional loan (term loan repayment over 5-7 years typically)
coverage: Over 1 lakh SC/ST MSEs supported through training, subsidy and procurement handholding since 2016; government procurement from SC/ST MSEs is tracked against the 4% mandate under the Public Procurement Policy
application_mode: Online registration on the SC-ST Hub portal; SCLCSS applications routed offline through the prime lending institution (bank) to SIDBI/NABARD
documents_required: Udyam Registration certificate; SC/ST caste certificate of proprietor/directors; ownership proof showing 51%+ SC/ST shareholding; PAN; GST; project report; machinery quotations/invoices for SCLCSS; loan sanction letter; bank account
helpline: SC-ST Hub helpline (Ministry of MSME); offices in major cities including Delhi
key_features: One-stop support system for SC/ST entrepreneurs; addresses the 4% public procurement mandate; includes the biggest SC/ST capital subsidy (25%, up to Rs 25 lakh); training and market access through NSIC/GeM
recent_updates: Scheme extended to 2025-26 with about Rs 588 crore outlay; GeM/NSIC onboarding and vendor-development programmes expanded in 2024-26; SCLCSS disbursals tracked on the MSME MIS portal

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
aliases: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy; SC ST capital subsidy 25%
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (sub-scheme under National SC-ST Hub)
implementing_agency: Prime Lending Institutions (banks) with nodal agencies SIDBI and NABARD; subsidy released through PFMS
launched_year: 2016 (sub-scheme of the National SC-ST Hub)
target_groups: SC/ST owned micro and small enterprises (manufacturing and services)
age_criteria: 18 years and above (proprietor/directors)
income_limit: No income ceiling
other_eligibility: Micro or small enterprise with valid Udyam Registration and at least 51% SC/ST ownership; institutional term loan sanctioned for purchase of new plant and machinery/equipment; no sector-specific restriction; SC/ST units upgraded to medium within 3 years remain eligible
exclusions: Second-hand machinery; enterprises without institutional finance; applicants who already got a similar capital subsidy (no dual benefit)
benefits_summary: Capital subsidy to reduce the cost of new plant and machinery financed by a bank/institution, improving the viability of SC/ST manufacturing and service units
benefit_amount: 25% capital subsidy on the institutional loan amount, capped at Rs 25,00,000 per enterprise (eligible term loan typically up to Rs 1 crore)
funding_pattern: 100% Central; disbursed through SIDBI/NABARD to the lending bank account of the beneficiary
interest_rate: Not applicable (bank interest applies; subsidy reduces effective cost)
repayment: As per the underlying term loan (usually 5 to 7 years)
coverage: Thousands of SC/ST MSEs given capital subsidy for modernisation since 2017-18
application_mode: Offline: obtain bank term loan, then the bank forwards the subsidy application to the nodal agency (SIDBI/NABARD) on the MSME MIS portal
documents_required: Udyam Registration; PAN; SC/ST caste certificate of all partners/directors; partnership deed or MOA/AOA; proof of 51%+ SC/ST shareholding; machinery/equipment invoices and payment receipts; bank sanction letter
helpline: SC-ST Hub helpline; MSME Development Institutes (MSME-DIs)
key_features: Highest-value capital subsidy available to SC/ST MSMEs; works only with bank finance (not on cash purchases); applies to manufacturing and service machinery/technology upgradation
recent_updates: Subsidy claims continue under NSSH till 2025-26; MSME Ministry has pushed awareness campaigns through MSME-DIs and state SC/ST corporations in 2024-26

scheme_name: Stand-Up India Scheme
aliases: Stand Up India loan; SC ST woman entrepreneur loan 10 lakh to 1 crore
nodal_ministry: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
implementing_agency: All scheduled commercial banks (public and private) - over 1.25 lakh branches; SIDBI operates the Standup Mitra handholding portal
launched_year: 5 April 2016
target_groups: SC, ST and women entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises
age_criteria: 18 years and above
income_limit: No income ceiling
other_eligibility: SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneur; greenfield project (first venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activity); for non-individual entities at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be with SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneurs; borrower must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
exclusions: Expansion of existing business; retail trading restricted in certain years; persons with existing bank defaults
benefits_summary: Composite bank loan (term loan plus working capital) for new enterprises, with collateral-free credit up to Rs 1 crore covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India Loans, plus Rupay debit card and handholding support through the Standup Mitra portal
benefit_amount: Composite loan of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore per borrower (loan limit raised/announced to Rs 2 crore under the 2025 relaunch for eligible categories - confirm with the bank). Margin money 25% of project cost, of which at least 10% must come from the borrower; the rest can come from convergence with other schemes
funding_pattern: Bank credit with credit guarantee support from the Government of India (CGTMSE/NCGTC)
interest_rate: Bank rate linked to MCLR/repo - normally the lowest applicable rate for that loan category; no collateral required up to Rs 1 crore
repayment: Up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months
coverage: Over 2.5 lakh loans target across bank branches; each branch is expected to finance at least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur
application_mode: Apply at any scheduled commercial bank branch or online through the Standup Mitra portal; SIDBI provides handholding
documents_required: Caste certificate (for SC/ST), identity and address proof, PAN, Aadhaar, business plan/project report, quotation for machinery, bank statements, proof of business premises
helpline: Standup Mitra helpline (SIDBI); bank branch managers
key_features: Dedicated credit line for SC/ST and women first-generation entrepreneurs; collateral-free; every bank branch has a target; composite loan structure; handholding portal with training material
recent_updates: Scheme relaunched with an enhanced loan ceiling (announced up to Rs 2 crore) and expanded skill modules in 2025; government has asked banks to speed up SC/ST borrower targeting

nodal_ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

age_criteria: 18 to 45 years
income_limit: Target-group based eligibility (no separate income ceiling in the main guidelines)
other_eligibility: Persons from SC/OBC/DNT/EBC/sanitation-worker families seeking wage or self-employment; selection through empanelled training partners; courses of 3 weeks (short-term), 3-6 months (upgradation) and 1 year (long-term/entrepreneurship)

scheme_name: UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Candidates
aliases: post doctoral fellowship SC ST; UGC PDF SC ST amount
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Education (University Grants Commission)
implementing_agency: University Grants Commission directly to fellows through universities/colleges
launched_year: Running since the 1990s-2000s; award rates revised with effect from 1 December 2014 (and later)
target_groups: Unemployed SC/ST candidates holding a PhD who want to do advanced research
age_criteria: Up to 50 years for men and up to 55 years for women (relaxation for PwD as per norms)
income_limit: No income ceiling - the candidate must be unemployed and not drawing any other fellowship/salary
other_eligibility: PhD degree in any subject; at least 50% marks at graduation and 55% at post-graduation; research to be conducted at a UGC-recognised university/college/institute of national importance; NOC from the proposed research centre needed
exclusions: Candidates already in employment or receiving another fellowship must resign before joining; fellowship terminates on resignation; no extension beyond the sanctioned duration
benefits_summary: Monthly post-doctoral fellowship for 5 years, contingency grant for research expenses, HRA as per institution rules and escort/reader assistance for persons with disabilities - all through DBT
benefit_amount: Rs 38,800 per month for the first two years and Rs 46,500 per month from the third year; contingency grant Rs 50,000 per year; escort/reader assistance Rs 2,000 per month for PwD candidates; duration 5 years with no extension
funding_pattern: 100% Central (UGC)
coverage: Slots vary each year (UGC announces the number in each cycle); reserved exclusively for SC and ST candidates
application_mode: Online application on the UGC portal when the call is announced; screening plus expert-committee interview
documents_required: Caste certificate (SC/ST); PhD degree/provisional certificate; UG and PG marksheets; NOC from the research centre; bank account; Aadhaar; research proposal
helpline: UGC scholarship/fellowship helpdesk, New Delhi
key_features: The highest-value research fellowship exclusively for SC/ST candidates; supports post-PhD research for 5 years; higher second-phase rate; strong pathway into academia
recent_updates: Rates continue at Rs 38,800/Rs 46,500 per month with Rs 50,000 annual contingency; applications invited in UGC cycles; Aadhaar-based DBT and 3-monthly institutional verification for continuity

scheme_name: Tuition fee waiver, free messing and pocket allowance for SC/ST/PwD students in IITs, NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutions
aliases: IIT SC ST fee waiver; NIT free messing SC ST; tuition waiver SC ST IIT
state_ut: All India (all IITs, NITs, IIITs, IIESTs and other centrally funded technical institutions)
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
implementing_agency: Individual IITs, NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutions
scheme_type: Institution-level fee waiver mandated by the Ministry of Education
launched_year: 2005-06 (fee waiver) with enhanced benefits from 2016 and extended for 2021-26, continuing
target_groups: SC, ST and PwD students (UG and PG) admitted to centrally funded technical institutions
age_criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines
income_limit: Tuition waiver is available to all SC/ST/PwD students; free messing, hostel rent exemption and pocket allowance are means-linked (commonly family income up to Rs 5 lakh; some institutes extend support up to Rs 8 lakh)
other_eligibility: Admission through JoSAA/JEE or the institute's own admission process; caste/disability certificate submitted to the institute's academic/financial aid office; registration and academic progress norms apply
exclusions: Waiver does not cover hostel/mess charges beyond the scheme design in all institutes; benefits are for the standard duration of the programme; lapses if the student drops out or fails to maintain registration
benefits_summary: Full tuition fee exemption for SC/ST/PwD students, plus (for means-qualifying students) free basic messing, hostel room-rent exemption and a monthly pocket allowance - making premier technical education nearly free for SC/ST students
benefit_amount: Full tuition waiver (worth about Rs 8-10 lakh over a 4-year B.Tech); free basic messing (worth about Rs 40,000-60,000 per year at most institutes); hostel rent exemption; pocket allowance of about Rs 250-500 per month, and up to about Rs 1,000 per month at some institutes such as IIT Delhi for income up to Rs 8 lakh
funding_pattern: 100% Central through the institutions' internal fee waiver and financial aid budgets
coverage: Thousands of SC/ST students in every admission batch across the 23 IITs, 31 NITs, 25+ IIITs and other CFTIs
application_mode: Automatic on admission - student submits the caste certificate and income certificate at reporting/financial-aid office; no separate online scheme application
documents_required: SC/ST/PwD caste or disability certificate; income certificate (for means-linked benefits); admission/registration proof; bank account; Aadhaar
helpline: Academic/Financial Aid Office of the concerned institution
key_features: Not a classic 'apply-online' scheme - it is an automatic statutory benefit at CFTIs; free messing plus pocket allowance makes hostel life affordable; income-linked benefits for SC/ST up to Rs 5-8 lakh; very few eligible students claim it
recent_updates: Better-off families (income above Rs 5 lakh) pay a higher tuition slab in some institutions; SC/ST/PwD waiver continues; institutes have been asked to publicise the waiver to increase uptake among SC/ST students

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
aliases: Central Sector Scholarship college university students; CSSS scholarship
nodal_ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education directly through the National Scholarship Portal
launched_year: 2007-08 (revised rates and ceilings in 2019-20 and later)
target_groups: Meritorious students from all categories, including SC/ST, pursuing college/university education after Class 12
age_criteria: Up to 25 years at the time of first application
income_limit: Family annual income up to Rs 4,50,000
other_eligibility: Above the 80th percentile in the Class 12 board examination; pursuing a regular degree course (not correspondence); not holding any other scholarship
exclusions: Students in distance/open learning, and those drawing another central scholarship, are not eligible
benefits_summary: Annual scholarship for the entire duration of the degree course (top-up to other benefits), paid by DBT through the National Scholarship Portal
benefit_amount: Rs 12,000 per year in the first three years (graduation) and Rs 20,000 per year during PG for the top 4,000 rank holders, with lower slabs for other selected students as notified (rates revised periodically)
funding_pattern: 100% Central
coverage: Tens of thousands of students across India every year, including a large share of SC/ST students
application_mode: Online through the National Scholarship Portal with institute and State verification
documents_required: Class 12 marksheet; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; admission proof; caste certificate where claimed
helpline: NSP helpline 0120-6619540
key_features: Merit-cum-means scholarship open to all categories; specifically useful for SC/ST students above the 80th percentile who may not get category-specific help for general degree courses; can be clubbed with State schemes in some cases
recent_updates: Rates and income ceilings revised upward; applications through NSP only; renewal conditional on 60% marks and 75% attendance
